description_good_justification: README.md opening line succinctly states purpose: 'C2PA manifest embedding, hard binding, and verification for OpenType/TrueType (SFNT) fonts.' Cargo.toml description field matches.
interact_justification: README.md 'Quick Start' explains how to obtain the crate (crates.io, npm, PyPI); README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md explain how to give feedback (GitHub Issues) and contribute (fork, branch, PR).
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR. .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml define the issue process.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies concrete acceptance requirements: 'cargo test --all-features', 'cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings', 'cargo fmt --all -- --check', and Conventional Commits style for commit messages.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml: license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; both are OSI-approved FLOSS licenses. LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT present at repo root.
floss_license_osi_justification: Both MIT and Apache-2.0 are on the OSI-approved license list (https://opensource.org/licenses).
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md covers overview, what the crate does/does not do, quick start, design, and links; src/lib.rs has crate-level //! docs and #![warn(missing_docs)] enforcing per-item documentation.
documentation_interface_justification: Public API (embed_manifest, reserve_manifest, fill_manifest, read_manifest, read_manifest_uri, verify, validate, data_hash_ranges) is documented with /// doc comments in src/*.rs and published to docs.rs (badge in README.md, docs.rs config in Cargo.toml [package.metadata.docs.rs]).
sites_https_justification: Repo URL is https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-fonts; crates.io, docs.rs, and npm distribution links in README.md are all https. No plain-http URLs found via grep of README.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/SECURITY.md/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-fonts: has_issues=true) and is publicly searchable, URL-addressable, and requires no proprietary client. GitHub Discussions is not enabled, but Issues alone satisfies this criterion.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and commit messages are in English; issue templates do not restrict report language.
maintained_justification: git log shows 34 commits between 2026-07-13 and 2026-08-22 (most recent commit 343a144 on 2026-08-22, within days of today 2026-08-26); two tagged releases (v0.2.0, v0.3.0); Dependabot PRs are being actively merged (gh pr list shows merges through 2026-08-10 and open dependency PRs awaiting merge).
repo_public_justification: gh repo view writerslogic/c2pa-fonts reports visibility=PUBLIC, isPrivate=false, at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-fonts.
repo_track_justification: Git repository; `git log --format='%an <%ae> %ad'` shows author, email, and date for every commit (e.g. David Condrey <davidcondrey@me.com>, dependabot[bot]).
repo_interim_justification: 34 commits exist between the two tagged releases v0.2.0 (2026-07-13) and v0.3.0 (2026-08-03), and further interim commits after v0.3.0 up to 343a144 (2026-08-22); not squashed to release-only commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses git, a distributed VCS (.git/ directory present, git remote origin git@github.com:writerslogic/c2pa-fonts.git).
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version = "0.3.0"; git tags v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 correspond to distinct, unique released versions on crates.io per the README crates.io badge.
version_semver_justification: Version 0.3.0 and tags v0.2.0/v0.3.0 follow strict SemVer (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), consistent with Cargo/crates.io convention.
version_tags_justification: `git tag` lists v0.2.0 and v0.3.0, matching Cargo.toml history and GitHub Releases (gh release list shows both).
release_notes_justification: gh release view v0.3.0 shows a human-readable, categorized (Added/Changed/Documentation) changelog body, generated by git-cliff (cliff.toml, .github/workflows/changelog.yml) from Conventional Commits rather than a raw commit log dump.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release to date (gh api .../security-advisories returns an empty list, no CVEs associated with this project); N/A per criterion.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml; CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' section documents the process.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues (has_issues=true) is the issue tracker used for individual bug/feature items, evidenced by .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ configs.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: `gh issue list -R writerslogic/c2pa-fonts --state all` returns zero non-PR issues filed to date; with no bug reports received in the project's lifetime (repo created 2026-07-13), the 'majority acknowledged' condition is vacuously satisfied.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met — flag for maintainer confirmation if/when real reports arrive.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: No enhancement requests have been filed via Issues to date (same evidence as report_responses); vacuously satisfied with no backlog of unanswered requests.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, searchable, permanently archived history of reports and responses at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-fonts/issues.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: GitHub Security Advisories (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-fonts/security/advisories/new) or email admin@writerslogic.com; linked from README.md '## Security' section.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explicitly offers two private channels: GitHub private security advisories and email to admin@writerslogic.com, with guidance on what to include.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received (gh api .../security-advisories returns an empty list; no security-advisory GitHub issues found); N/A per criterion, no reports to measure response time against.
build_justification: Standard Cargo build: `cargo build` (documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md); .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo check --all-features` on every push/PR, and release.yml builds crates.io/wasm/PyO3 artifacts.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack and maturin for the wasm and Python bindings respectively — all conventional tools for this language ecosystem.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, wasm-bindgen, and maturin are all FLOSS; no proprietary build tool is required (verified via Cargo.toml dependencies and .github/workflows/*.yml build steps).
test_justification: FLOSS test suite: unit tests embedded in src/*.rs (#[cfg(test)] modules in reader.rs, sfnt.rs, table.rs, writer.rs, verify.rs, error.rs) plus tests/roundtrip.rs integration test. CONTRIBUTING.md documents `cargo test` and `cargo test --all-features` to run them.
test_invocation_justification: Tests are run with the standard `cargo test` invocation for Rust, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and executed identically in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
test_most_justification: grep -c '#[test]' across src/*.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs shows tests in every core module (sfnt.rs: 9, writer.rs: 11, table.rs: 6, reader.rs: 4, verify.rs: 4, error.rs: 2) plus a real-font round-trip integration test (tests/roundtrip.rs, 169 lines) covering embed/reserve/fill/validate against actual .ttf/.otf files installed in CI (ci.yml installs fonts-dejavu-core, fonts-freefont-otf).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml 'test' job runs `cargo test` and `cargo test --features validation` on every push to main and every pull request.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2 explicitly instructs contributors to 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features.'
tests_are_added_justification: Recent commits show tests accompanying functional changes, e.g. commit 42e1d64 'feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests' added tests/roundtrip.rs alongside the feature.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the test-addition policy directly in the contribution instructions (step 2 of 'Submitting Changes').
warnings_justification: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings` (Rust's standard FLOSS linter) and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` on every push/PR; src/lib.rs also sets #![warn(missing_docs)] and #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
warnings_fixed_justification: CI enforces `clippy -- -D warnings`, which fails the build on any warning, so warnings cannot merge unaddressed; current main (commit 343a144) passes CI per the README CI badge.
warnings_strict_justification: clippy is run with `-D warnings` (deny, the strictest common setting) across `--all-features`, plus `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and `#![warn(missing_docs)]` in src/lib.rs for additional strictness beyond default lints.
know_secure_design_justification: src/lib.rs:24 `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` rules out memory-unsafe code by construction. SECURITY.md's Supply-chain security section documents mitigations for common attack classes: GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHAs (against tag-mutation attacks), OpenSSF Scorecard, Dependency Review, and Dependabot running in CI, and build provenance on releases where the registry supports it.
know_common_errors_justification: SECURITY.md's Supply-chain security section documents specific mitigations for common attack classes: GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHAs (against tag-mutation attacks), OpenSSF Scorecard, Dependency Review, and Dependabot running in CI to catch known-vulnerable dependencies, and build provenance on releases.
crypto_published_justification: This crate implements no cryptography itself; it only embeds/extracts opaque C2PA manifest bytes. Signature verification is delegated to the optional c2pa crate (Cargo.toml: c2pa = { version = "0.89", features = ["rust_native_crypto"] }), which is out of this repo's scope.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic operations are performed in this crate's own code; all COSE/X.509 crypto is delegated to the external c2pa crate via the optional 'validation' feature (see README.md 'What this crate does — and does not' table, steps 3-4 owned by c2pa-rs).
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptography is implemented in this repository.
crypto_keylength_justification: No cryptographic key generation or key-length defaults exist in this repository; delegated entirely to the optional c2pa dependency.
crypto_working_justification: No cryptographic algorithm selection occurs in this repository's code.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic algorithm selection occurs in this repository's code.
crypto_pfs_justification: This crate performs no key agreement or network handshake; not applicable.
crypto_password_storage_justification: This crate has no authentication or password-storage functionality; it is a font-file manipulation library.
crypto_random_justification: This crate generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; not applicable.
delivery_mitm_justification: Package is distributed via crates.io, npm, and PyPI, all served over HTTPS; the GitHub source repo is cloned over https/ssh. No plain-http distribution channel exists (verified via README.md install instructions).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check delivered over plain HTTP is used; distribution is exclusively via HTTPS-backed registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) and .github/workflows/release.yml uses actions/attest-build-provenance for build provenance attestation rather than a bare unsigned hash.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-fonts/security-advisories returns an empty list and gh api .../vulnerability-alerts returns HTTP 204 (Dependabot security alerts enabled); no known unpatched medium+ vulnerability has been reported against this project. Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) files weekly dependency-update PRs and several have already been merged promptly (e.g. PR #7 'Aikido AI Fix for 3rd party Github Actions should be pinned', merged 2026-08-03, and commit 46ef9bd 'ci(security): pin actions by SHA and drop GITHUB_TOKEN to read').
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported against this project to date (empty security-advisories list); the one security-flagged finding on record (unpinned third-party GitHub Actions, PR #7) was fixed the same day it was raised (2026-08-03), evidencing a fast response pattern.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: `git log -p --all | grep -iE 'AKIA|BEGIN (RSA|EC|OPENSSH) PRIVATE KEY|api[_-]?key|secret'` across full history returned no matches. release.yml documents required secrets (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN) as GitHub Actions repository secrets, not committed values.
static_analysis_justification: clippy (a FLOSS static analysis tool for Rust) is run in .github/workflows/ci.yml on `--all-features` before merge, and again as part of release.yml's validate/gate job before every tagged release.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: clippy's default and pedantic lint groups include checks for common correctness/soundness issues (e.g. arithmetic overflow patterns, indexing panics via clippy::indexing_slicing when enabled, suspicious casts); combined with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in src/lib.rs eliminating the memory-unsafety class outright, and OpenSSF Scorecard (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml) additionally analyzing the repo for supply-chain risk patterns.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI runs clippy with `-D warnings`, which blocks merge on any finding, so medium+ findings cannot land unaddressed; commit cde4c7a 'chore: harden lints, docs, and CI' shows lint findings being fixed directly.
static_analysis_often_justification: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs clippy on every push to main and every pull request (not just before releases), satisfying 'every commit'.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. cargo-fuzz, AFL, sanitizers) is configured anywhere in .github/workflows/ or the repo; no fuzz/ directory exists. This is a SUGGESTED criterion and its absence does not block Passing level, but it is honestly Unmet.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: src/lib.rs declares #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and `grep -rn unsafe src/*.rs` finds only that one forbid directive; no memory-unsafe (C/C++) code exists in this crate, so dynamic memory-safety tooling is not applicable.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis configuration exists in the repo (see dynamic_analysis above), so no assertion-enabling config exists either. SUGGESTED criterion, honestly Unmet.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is run against this project, so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to have fixed or left unfixed.
